newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corporate debt issuers pause for election day.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corporate debt issuers pause for election day.

text.p: Corporate debt new issue activiity paused briefly on Tuesday as Americans cast their votes for the next U.S. President and Congress, but players said more supply is hanging in the wings.
"It's pretty quiet right now but there's a lot of behind the scenes structuring of deals going on," said one high-grade syndicate source.

Issuers are expected to take a temporary breather as the market digests Tuesday's U.S. election results, using the time to structure new deals amid a favorable interest rate environment, dealers said.
With U.S. Treasury yields at their lowest levels since spring, opportunistic issuers should continue to push fresh supply into the market, dealers said.
Currently, the 30-year U.S. Treasury bond is trading up 22/32 at 101-26/32 to yield 6.61 percent.
"The White House isn't changing tenants...this is going to give the market more of a positive tone," one high-grade syndicate source said.
"I walked in this morning and within one hour the stock market was up 30 points, the bond market was up almost a half a point...it's just very positive so far," he added.
At 1116 EST/1616 GMT, the Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 28 points at 6070.38.

Meanwhile, on Tuesday, CIT Group Holdings jumped on the new issue bandwagon to price $100 million in Aa3/A-plus rated two-year notes to yield 17 basis points over Treasuries. Lehman Brothers was lead underwriter on the deal.
Still, another $1.0 billion in new investment grade corporate debt is on the horizon, dealers added.
Korea Development Bank is expected to price $500 million in A1/AA-minus 10-year debt, sources said.
Western Mining Corp Holdings Ltd is expected to price $300 million in 10-year debt, sources said, while Goodyear Tire & Rubber Co is expected to bring its $250 million debt issue this week.
Turning to the high-yield sector, approximately $1.5 billion in private placement debt offerings are gearing up to come to market, dealers said.
YPF SA is expected to price $200 million in senior notes due 2001 via Merrill Lynch & Co.
Olympus Communications may price $200 million in 144A senior notes via Goldman Sachs & Co.
Parker Drilling Co is expected to issue $275 million in 144A senior notes due 2006 via Jeffries & Co.
Abraxas Petroleum Corp is expected to issue $200 million in eight-year 144A notes via BT Securities. Price talk on the issue is seen at 10.75-11.0 percent, sources said.
Amtrol Inc may price $100 million in 144A senior subordinated notes due 2006, sources added.
Pillowtex Corp may issue $125 million in 144A senior subordinated notes due 2006 via Nationsbanc Capital Markets.
Cole National Corp is expected to price $140 million in 144Asenior subordinated notes due 2006 via CIBC Wood Gundy.
Dollar Financial Group and IMED Corp are also expected to issue 144A debt near term.
--Nancy Leinfuss, 212-859-1675
